name: Wall Sit
description: The wall sit is an isometric lower body exercise in which the lifter holds a squat position with the back flat against a wall, thighs parallel to the floor, and knees at 90°. Because it requires no movement, it trains muscular endurance and time-under-tension of the quadriceps. It is used for rehabilitation, athletic conditioning, and as a simple test of quad endurance.

execution.starting_position: Stand with your back flat against a smooth wall. Walk your feet forward until they are approximately 60–90 cm from the wall.
execution.setup_instructions: Find a smooth, flat wall. Wear shoes with grip. The feet should be shoulder-width apart and directly below the knees when in position.
steps: Step 1: Slide your back down the wall until your thighs are parallel to the floor and your knees are at 90°.
Step 2: Ensure your knees are directly over your ankles — not in front of them.
Step 3: Keep your back flat against the wall throughout. Do not lean forward.
Step 4: Hold the position for the target duration while breathing steadily.
Step 5: To exit, slide back up the wall to standing or step forward.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe steadily throughout the hold. Do not hold the breath for extended durations — this increases blood pressure unnecessarily.
common_mistakes: Knees extending past the toes due to feet placed too close to the wall
Back peeling away from the wall due to core fatigue
Thighs not reaching parallel — reduces quad demand significantly
safety_considerations: Those with knee pain should check that knees track over toes and that feet are positioned appropriately
Avoid performing to failure on a slippery floor
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Thighs must reach parallel to the floor. Anything shallower significantly reduces the training stimulus.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Isometric hold — measure in seconds or minutes rather than reps
coaching_cues: Thighs parallel — don't cheat with a shallow squat
Back flat to the wall at all times
Breathe steadily — don't hold your breath
